questions.stem: The long fibre that carries an impulse away from the cell body of a neurone is the
questions.explanation: The axon is the outgoing fibre. Dendrites bring impulses in; the synapse is the gap to the next cell; myelin is the insulating sheath wrapped around many axons, not the fibre itself.

distractorRationale.a: Dendrites receive impulses and pass them towards the cell body
distractorRationale.c: A synapse is a gap, not a fibre
distractorRationale.d: Myelin is insulation around the axon

questions.stem: The central nervous system consists of the
questions.explanation: By definition the CNS is the brain plus the spinal cord. Cranial and spinal nerves make up the peripheral nervous system. Sense organs are receptors; muscles and glands are effectors.

distractorRationale.b: Those nerves are the peripheral nervous system
distractorRationale.c: Sense organs detect stimuli but are not the CNS
distractorRationale.d: Muscles and glands are effectors at the end of a pathway

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Nervous System and Sense Organs

questions.stem: In a spinal reflex, the correct order of structures is

options.text: effector → motor neurone → receptor → sensory neurone
receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone in the spinal cord → motor neurone → effector
receptor → motor neurone → brain → sensory neurone → effector

questions.explanation: The impulse starts at the receptor, travels in on a sensory neurone, crosses synapses in the spinal cord via a relay neurone, and leaves on a motor neurone to the effector. The brain is informed but is not required for the arc itself, which is why the response is so fast.

distractorRationale.a: This sequence runs the wrong way, from effector to receptor
distractorRationale.c: The motor neurone is last, not second, and a spinal reflex does not have to go through the brain
distractorRationale.d: The brain does not start a simple withdrawal reflex

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Nervous System and Sense Organs

questions.stem: When the eye focuses on a near object, the

options.text: ciliary muscles relax, suspensory ligaments become taut and the lens thins
ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments slacken and the lens becomes fatter

questions.explanation: Accommodation for near vision needs a more convex lens. Contraction of the ciliary muscle reduces tension in the suspensory ligaments, so the elastic lens bulges. The opposite set of changes is used for distant objects. The iris controls light intensity, not focal length.

distractorRationale.a: This is accommodation for a distant object, not a near one
distractorRationale.c: The pupil never closes completely in normal vision; the iris does not focus the image
distractorRationale.d: The optic nerve transmits impulses; it does not change length to focus

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Nervous System and Sense Organs

questions.stem: The part of the ear that converts sound vibrations into nerve impulses is the
questions.explanation: Hair cells in the organ of Corti inside the cochlea transduce vibration into electrical impulses that travel in the auditory nerve. The pinna and tympanum only collect and transmit sound; the semicircular canals detect rotational movement for balance, not sound.

distractorRationale.a: The pinna funnels sound into the canal; it does not generate impulses
distractorRationale.b: The tympanum vibrates but does not convert the vibration into a nerve impulse
distractorRationale.d: Semicircular canals serve balance, not hearing

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Nervous System and Sense Organs

questions.stem: Rods differ from cones in that rods

options.text: detect colour in bright light and are concentrated at the fovea
function in dim light and do not distinguish colour
are found only in the blind spot

questions.explanation: Rods are highly sensitive, so they work in moonlight and at dusk, but they give only shades of grey. Cones need bright light, detect colour and are packed at the fovea. The blind spot has neither rods nor cones, which is why an image falling there is not seen.

distractorRationale.c: The optic nerve is formed by axons of ganglion cells, not by rods themselves
distractorRationale.d: The blind spot has no photoreceptors at all

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Nervous System and Sense Organs

questions.stem: A drug that blocks the release of transmitter at synapses in the spinal cord would most directly prevent

options.text: detection of a stimulus by a skin receptor
passage of the impulse from a sensory neurone to a motor neurone in a reflex
refraction of light by the cornea

questions.explanation: A reflex depends on chemical transmission across spinal synapses. If transmitter cannot be released, the sensory neurone still fires but the relay and motor neurones are not stimulated, so the effector never receives the command. Axonal conduction and receptors do not use that synaptic transmitter step.

distractorRationale.a: Receptors start the impulse before any synapse in the cord is involved
distractorRationale.c: Myelin speeds axonal conduction electrically; it is not the synaptic chemical step
distractorRationale.d: The cornea is part of the eye's optics, unrelated to spinal synapses

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Nervous System and Sense Organs

questions.stem: A patient hears well but cannot keep balance when walking in the dark. Which structures are most likely damaged?
questions.explanation: Hearing is intact, so the cochlea, tympanum and ossicles are working. Balance in the dark depends on the semicircular canals (and related vestibular organs), because vision cannot then compensate. Cones affect colour vision in bright light, not body equilibrium.

distractorRationale.a: Cochlear damage would impair hearing, which this patient has not lost
distractorRationale.c: Damage here would reduce hearing by blocking sound transmission
distractorRationale.d: Cones are photoreceptors; they do not maintain balance
